title: Missale Syriacum (Rome Propaganda, 1843) — Anaphora of St. James Core — independent pixel-collation review
scope: Bounded constituent of the six core prayers of the Anaphora of St. James (Preface, Sanctus, Post-Sanctus, Institution Narrative, Anamnesis, and Epiclesis) in Classical Syriac (syr), reading the right-hand Syriac column on bilingual Syriac/Garshuni pages (PDF 135, 136, 139, 140 L1) and full-width Syriac on monolingual pages (PDF 136 bottom, 138, 140), excluding the scan-degraded red-ink opening Dialogue line on PDF 135, the Crucifixion engraving plate at PDF 137, Garshuni columns, rubrics, and post-epiclesis diptychs.
method: Independent pixel-level visual inspection of all rendered facsimile pages by independent-collator-v2-syriac (distinct from drafter lane-t2-syriac) on 2026-11-25. Applied 4 pixel-verified correction(s) relative to initial draft; verified every unit boundary, page account (1..279), and SHA-256 hash.
normalization_limit: Pure consonantal Classical Syriac Unicode (U+0710..U+072C, UTF-8 NFC) with single ASCII spaces between words and single LF (\n) line endings, one canonical liturgical unit per line.; All West Syriac vowel points, seyame (U+0308), qushshaya/rukkakha, punctuation marks, liturgical crosses, kashidas, catchwords, running heads, signature marks, and page numbers are omitted for scan-safe cross-edition diffing.; Rubrics (red or black stage directions), speaker labels (priest/deacon/people, including abbreviated ܟܗ̄), editorial 'etc.' cues (ܘܫܪ / ܗܟܢܐ), silent/intervening rubrical cues, non-text plates, blank leaves, and parallel Garshuni/Arabic columns are excluded.; Printed historical orthography, abbreviations (such as ܩܕ for ܩܕܝܫܐ, ܩܘܪܝ for ܩܘܪܝܐܠܝܣܘܢ, and abbreviated Sanctus/Anamnesis incipits), omissions, and additions are preserved verbatim without harmonizing or supplying words from memory.
review_limit: Complete declared constituent only, not whole-book transcription or diplomatic typography.
